Review.ItemLabel: UAT-3: Toggle Availability button activates an unavailable product and the change persists after reload

Steps.Action: CLICK INPUT with label "Email address" and enter "admin@acmecoffee.com"
CLICK BUTTON with caption "Send sign-in link"

Verifications.Text: Product detail for 'Blonde Roast - Decaf - Espresso' (product #17, seeded as unavailable) loads. ACTIVATE button is visible (indicating the product is currently unavailable).
The page updates immediately. The button label changes from 'ACTIVATE' to 'DEACTIVATE' - indicating the product is now available. No error is shown.
After reloading the product detail, the toggle button shows 'DEACTIVATE' (the product is now available). The availability change persisted across navigation.

Review.Feedback: Judgment item - the button label change from ACTIVATE to DEACTIVATE is the key visual signal. The label 'DEACTIVATE' is not in the component catalog (catalog was crawled against a deactivated product, so only ACTIVATE appears), making the post-click label a human judgment step. Persona: admin@acmecoffee.com. Product #17 = 'Blonde Roast - Decaf - Espresso' (IsAvailable=false in seed data). Run against a fresh seeded DB or manually run DEACTIVATE on Product #17 afterward to restore the seeded unavailable state.

Review.ItemLabel: UAT-6: Orders status workflow button transitions the order to the next status

Steps.Action: CLICK INPUT with label "Email address" and enter "admin@acmecoffee.com"
CLICK BUTTON with caption "Send sign-in link"

Verifications.Text: Order #355 detail loads. Note the current status chip. Status workflow buttons (e.g., SHIPPED, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED) are visible in the action row depending on current order status.
The status chip updates immediately to show 'Shipped'. No error is shown. The SHIPPED button may become hidden or disabled (order is now in shipped state). The transition is server-persisted.

Review.Feedback: Judgment item - the status chip label after transition is the key visual signal. If Order #355 is already in 'Shipped' or a terminal state from prior UAT runs, use any order from /orders list that has a non-terminal status (not Delivered or Cancelled) and click its available transition button. The catalog shows SHIPPED and CANCELLED buttons for /orders/{OrderId}. Persona: admin@acmecoffee.com. The SHIPPED status transition is persisted to the DB. Order #355 will need to remain in a non-terminal state for re-runs; run against a fresh seeded DB or use a different qualifying order.

Review.ItemLabel: UAT-10: Add a product line item to an order via the nested Items tab, save the parent order, and verify persistence

Steps.Action: CLICK INPUT with label "Email address" and enter "admin@acmecoffee.com"
CLICK BUTTON with caption "Send sign-in link"

Verifications.Text: Order #355 detail loads. An 'ITEMS' tab is visible. The current item count is shown in the tab label (e.g., 'ITEMS (1)'). Note this count.

A product picker dialog opens showing available products. Select 'Medium Roast - Regular - Drip' from the list and confirm the selection. The dialog closes. The ITEMS tab count increments by 1. The parent SAVE button becomes enabled (the in-memory order is now dirty).
The parent order saves. SAVE button becomes disabled. The ITEMS tab count still shows the updated count (original + 1).

After reloading the order, the ITEMS tab count includes the newly added item. The 'Medium Roast - Regular - Drip' row appears in the items grid under the ITEMS tab. The add persisted to the database via the parent save.

Review.Feedback: Judgment item - the nested item form controls (product picker dialog, row expansion form) are behind click-driven navigation and are not in the component catalog. Step 7 opens the ADD PRODUCT dialog (CLICK BUTTON 'ADD PRODUCT' is catalog-grounded for /orders/{OrderId}); the dialog interaction and subsequent SAVE are visual confirmations. The W2-compiled test will partially exercise this item (opening the dialog) but will not complete the full dialog interaction. Persona: admin@acmecoffee.com. The added OrderItem and parent Order save are persisted to the DB. Order #355 will have one more item after UAT; run against a fresh seeded DB if re-running this item.
